subject.title: [Feature]: Skill author-defined setup hook (run skill-supplied script on install/update)

question: Should OpenClaw make skill-authored setup execution a native install/update lifecycle hook, keep it as an explicit ClawHub/admin plugin workflow, or reject this execution surface for now?
rationale: Running skill-supplied scripts with selected environment values changes the host execution and credential boundary, and automation cannot choose the acceptable consent, logging, env, and failure semantics for maintainers.

options.title: Design native lifecycle hook
options.body: Add a security-reviewed `setup.script` lifecycle contract for install/update with explicit consent, path containment, timeout ownership, redacted output, and env sanitizer behavior.

options.title: Use ClawHub plugin path
options.body: Declare the published `skills-setup` plugin plus stable SDK helpers as the supported route, and document that setup is an explicit admin action rather than automatic lifecycle execution.

options.title: Decline setup execution
options.body: Reject skill-supplied setup execution in OpenClaw and keep wrappers or external operator workflows as the supported pattern.

recommendation.title: Design native lifecycle hook
recommendation.body: Add a security-reviewed `setup.script` lifecycle contract for install/update with explicit consent, path containment, timeout ownership, redacted output, and env sanitizer behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This crosses ClawHub skill install behavior, setup reliability, and plugin/core boundary policy, all tied to this owner candidate in history and VISION-level direction.
